Hon'ble Subhash Vidyarthi,J.
1.

Heard Sri Suhaib Ashraf, Advocate holding brief of Shri Pranjal Krishna, learned counsel for the applicant as well as Shri Abhishek Kumar Singh, the learned AGA for the State and perused the records.
2.

The instant application has been filed by the applicant seeking anticipatory bail in Crl. Case No.1748 of 2017 (State Vs. Sanjeev Kumar Verma & Others) under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 I.P.C., arising out of Crime No.0049 of 2016, P.S. Lambhua, district Sultanpur.

sentences.text:
3. It is alleged in the prosecution case the complainant is co-owner of khasra No.87 Min, 96, 96cha,
91ka, 112kha, 112ga, 84ba, 112ka, 84, situated at village Gopalpur, Pargana Meeranpur, Tehsil Lambhua, district Sultanpur.
The accused persons are alleged to have sold the acquired land despite the ban imposed on sale-purchase and mutation of the acquired land and the mutation proceedings of the said land are going on.
It is further alleged that the accused persons have misled the Highway Authority of India, sold excess land than their share, in lieu of obtaining wrongful gain of compensation.

1 4.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the first information report was lodged on 6.2.2016.
The notification for acquisition of land was issued under relevant Act on 22.10.2013.
It is submitted that a perusal of the notification shows that except Gata No.87, none of the Gatas referred in the first information report are subject matter of the gazette notification.
Therefore, the entire story of the first information report is bogus.
As regards gata No.87, part of gata No.87 is involved in the notification.
The remaining part of gata No.87 which is in possession of the complainant has been left out.
The complainant and co-accused Sanjay Verma, Rajeev Verma & Dayawati Verma have been granted compensation way back in September, 2015.
This fact is evident from a perusal of the Form 11 issued for the purpose of land acquisition and the same has been obtained by the applicant under Right to Information Act.

5. It is submitted that even the registered sale deeds have been executed after September 2015,
precisely on 31.12.2015 and therefore, it cannot be said that in any manner the applicant has executed sale deed in lieu of obtaining compensation wrongfully.
It is further submitted that it is a clear case of blackmailing and harassment by the complainant.
The applicant has been implicated merely because he had witnessed the sale deed and has no criminal antecedents.
6. It is further submitted that the applicant has cooperated in the investigation.
Charge sheet has been filed.
He undertakes to cooperate in the trial.

Co-accused Rajeev Kumar Verma, Mahendra Kumar and Nitin Verma have already been granted anticipatory bail by means of orders dated 16.1.2023, 22.12.2023 and 19.05.2023 passed in Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application Nos.
98/2023, 3051/2023 and 1194/2023.
7.

entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: Having considered the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in view the fact that three co-accused persons have already been granted anticipatory bail in the present case, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be granted anticipatory bail in the present case 8.
Accordingly the anticipatory bail application is allowed.
